tasks.title: store::read — the GraphReader aggregate, GraphMeta, pool, ToolContext

details.goal: One trait with the 22 methods the seven handlers call, a `GraphMeta` that reads identity and generation, a per-root reader pool, and the `ToolContext` seam a handler receives.
details.contract:
Port `src/shared/store/read/reader.ts` (544 lines) as a trait plus its SQLite implementation. Exact method set:
```rust
find_by_qn, find_by_name(name, kinds?), members(parent_id), nodes_by_file(file_id),
inbound(node_id, kinds?), outbound(node_id, kinds?), metrics_for(node_id),
rows_for_paths(prefixes), not_indexed_all(), not_indexed_count(), unresolved_for_files(file_ids),
file_by_path(path), all_files(), census_by_language(), tests_census(), meta_for(),
latest_generation(), removed_symbols_for(since_generation), entry_points(limit), hotspots(limit),
test_gaps(ids), read_node_fts(match_query, limit)
```
`meta_for()` returns `GraphMeta { schema_version, generation, generation_seq, indexer_state, consecutive_failures, project_name, project_root, project_branch, project_remote, embed_dim }`, reading the `meta` key/value rows with `Null` for an absent key (never an error). `latest_generation()` returns the `generation` row with the highest `seq`. `removed_symbols_for(gen)` reads tombstones. `entry_points(limit)` orders by `reachable_count` descending over `idx_metrics_entry` with `is_entry = 1`; `hotspots(limit)` — copy the TypeScript ORDER BY; `test_gaps(ids)` uses `idx_metrics_tested` and returns nothing when `ids` is empty without querying; `read_node_fts` is the ONLY place `MATCH` and `bm25(node_fts)` appear, ordered `bm25 ASC, in_degree DESC, id ASC` (score is raw bm25; smaller is better), reusing the ranked SELECT the TypeScript module defines.
`context.rs`: `ToolContext { reader: Rc<dyn GraphReader>, cursor: CursorFacade, log: Logger, now: fn() -> DateTime<Utc>, config: Rc<AppConfig>, db_size_bytes: u64 }` — six fields, no environment access, no connection. `pool.rs`: one reader per repository root keyed by canonical path, idle eviction without its own timer (the caller ticks).
Tests: a populated fixture asserting one non-empty answer per method, `meta_for` with a missing key, `test_gaps(&[])` performing zero queries (assert via the cache counters), and a pool that returns the same handle for the same root twice and another for a second root.
steps: Port reader.rs: row types, GraphMeta, then the aggregate trait with adapters over TASK-016/017's functions.
Port the four analytics queries (entry_points, hotspots, test_gaps, read_node_fts) verbatim, including the ranked SELECT constant.
Port context.rs as types only (the cursor facade trait, logger, clock).
Port pool.rs with keyed handles and idle eviction.
Write the per-method test over a hand-built fixture.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-store --test read_reader` exits 0 with at least 22 assertions (one per method).
Done when: `grep -rn 'MATCH node_fts\|bm25(' rust/crates` shows hits in `read/reader.rs` only, and `meta_for()` returns `None` (not an error) for a dropped `project_name` row.

tasks.title: Reader goldens: dump the TypeScript answers, compare the Rust ones

details.goal: Prove the Rust reader answers the same rows as the TypeScript reader on the same database, method by method, before any handler depends on it.
details.contract:
`scripts/parity/capture-reader-dump.ts` runs under bun against a fixture indexed by the TypeScript binary and writes `rust/tests/golden/reader/<fixture>.json`, one key per reader method with a deterministic projection:
`find_by_name("<a name that exists twice>")`, `find_by_qn("<qn>")`, `members(<class id>)`, `nodes_by_file(<file id>)`, `inbound`/`outbound` for a node with at least three edges, `metrics_for`, `rows_for_paths(["src"])` and `(["lib"])` on polyglot, `not_indexed_all`, `unresolved_for_files`, `file_by_path`, `all_files`, `census_by_language`, `tests_census`, `meta_for`, `latest_generation`, `removed_symbols_for(<generation>)`, `entry_points(5)`, `hotspots(5)`, `test_gaps(<three ids>)`, `read_node_fts("<a query that matches>", 5)`.
Projections must be stable across runs: ids included (they are rowids and must match only if the two implementations read the same database — which they do), timestamps excluded, and every list in its query order.
`rust/crates/sangkar-store/tests/reader_golden.rs` opens the same `graph.db` (path from an env var the test reads once, `SANGKAR_FIXTURE_DB`, and skipped with a clear message when unset), produces the identical projection through the Rust `GraphReader`, and compares it to the committed JSON with a structural diff that names the method and the first differing element.
Capture for both `polyglot` and `broken`. Do not hand-edit the goldens.
steps: Write the capture script with one deterministic projection per method.
Index both fixtures with the TypeScript binary and write the two golden files.
Write the Rust projection and the comparison test.
Run both and fix any reader mismatch by fixing the Rust query ordering/joins — never by relaxing the comparison.
Commit the goldens and document the `SANGKAR_FIXTURE_DB` contract in the test header.
details.verify:
`~/.bun/bin/bun run scripts/parity/capture-reader-dump.ts` exits 0 and writes two files under `rust/tests/golden/reader/`.
`SANGKAR_FIXTURE_DB=<path to a polyglot graph.db> cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-store --test reader_golden` exits 0 and reports 22 compared methods.
Done when: the comparison covers all 22 methods and a deliberately re-sorted `find_by_name` ordering makes it fail.
